source.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
source.authors: Nicholas Roberts; Ahmed Ahmed; Suhas Kotha; Percy Liang; Yu Wang; Alex Renda; Nitya Mani

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. There are minor PDF text-extraction and equation-formatting artifacts, but they do not prevent reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends language-model scaling analysis to synthetic rewriting, fitting and testing loss and compute-allocation forecasts in compute-limited and data-limited pretraining settings.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own experiments measure held-out BPB across model sizes, token counts, compute budgets, rewrite fractions, and data regimes. Cited scaling-law and synthetic-data results from other studies are not recorded as findings here. It does not test the effect of varying depth or width at a fixed parameter count; most runs use a specified Qwen3 width-to-depth rule.
record.test_reason: The paper fits Chinchilla-style loss surfaces in parameters and tokens. It forecasts held-out runs 33× beyond the fit range, fits compute-optimal N*/D* frontiers per evaluation and per corpus, and tests downstream BPB and accuracy forecasts. All of this is in a new setting: pretraining on synthetic-rewrite mixtures, with a data-limited repeated-data variant. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In the compute-limited setting, a fit made at small budgets picks the best rewrite fraction at 33× the compute, within 1.1% of predicted loss. The resulting 22B model beats its rewriter on 10 of 16 Paloma sources at about one-tenth of its compute. In the data-limited setting, held-out-budget optima and losses are predictable, and rewrites from a size-matched rewriter beat the best natural-only run at every size up to 3B. The authors caveat the FineWeb-Edu-only seed set, the four rewrite styles, and approximate compute accounting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Qwen3 pretraining and BPB measurements, adds a rewrite-dependent loss floor and data-limited repetition penalty, and charges approximate compute for generating rewrites. It is not a direct reproduction of the original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted allocation and optimum depend on evaluation task, source corpus, BPB versus accuracy criterion, rewrite fraction, and data-limited repetition-penalty form. The off-frontier fit also depends on including a curvature term.

fits_no_version.finding: The QA-optimal rewrite fraction at 1e22 is 0.749 under the BPB fit and 0.638 under the accuracy fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal data-mixture choices predicted by scaling fits depend on whether loss or accuracy is the criterion.

fits_no_version.finding: The DCLM floor-optimal rewrite fraction is about 0.078, with a 0.0058 BPB gain, smaller than on FineWeb-Edu.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefit of synthetic rewrites shrinks on stronger natural corpora.

record.problems: The study uses one primary natural corpus for its main experiments and four FinePhrase rewrite styles. Its compute accounting is approximate and excludes rewriter pretraining costs. The 10^22-FLOP compute-limited result is an extrapolation beyond the fitted training budgets, and the QA, Math, and Code large-budget forecasts have larger errors than Paloma. Some fitted asymptotic and repetition parameters are described as weakly identified.
record.rows_left_out: Individual points from the large IsoFLOP sweeps, the full per-source Paloma table, and the complete data-limited grid are not listed separately; the record includes the paper’s explicit aggregate fit and forecast results instead. Detailed source-by-source downstream scores and qualitative rewrite examples are omitted because they do not separately measure the scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: All of it. Depth is set by a fixed width-to-depth rule, and no fixed-N shape comparison is reported.
Image, video and other modalities; fine-tuning; transfer.
Separate parameter-only or token-only scans with the other factor unconstrained; corpora other than FineWeb-Edu, except the small DCLM ladder.
Extrapolation in the data-limited setting beyond 1.33×, and extrapolation on corpora other than FineWeb-Edu.
Allocation in the data-limited setting, where N is fixed.

missing.what: Forward leave-one-budget-out forecasts at 1.7–3.3× extrapolation, with mean errors from −0.21% to −1.32% (Table 8 rows other than 1e22).
Per-R Approach-2 token exponents of 0.45–0.57 against the shared 0.46, with per-R optima within 0.85–1.28× of the shared D*.
Surface-model ladder M1/M2/M3: F tests reject the shared center, but BIC favours it, and floor shifts agree within 0.005 BPB.
The natural-only token multiplier at 1e22 is 5.01× under the final fit but 12.17× under the 671-run fit, with a divergence point of 3.6e26 vs 1.75e24 FLOPs.
In-grid RMSE of the per-evaluation surfaces: Paloma 0.0148, QA 0.0195, Math 0.0301, Code 0.0681 BPB.
Approach-3 exponents α=0.205 and β=0.236; near-frontier RMSE 0.0096 over 296 runs.

record.verdict_notes: There are four corrections. (1) The data-limited rows (r5–r12) do not bear on V1 or V2: they are fixed-N, repeated-data runs with ≤1.33× extrapolation. (2) r14 and r24 do not bear on any version. (3) r4's N* of 22.39B conflicts with Table 10's 23.5B for Paloma. (4) The main surface includes the 1e22 hero run as an anchor, so only Table 8's forward forecast is a clean V2 test. The fitted split, N∝C^0.54 and D∝C^0.46, sits near Hoffmann, not Kaplan, for Paloma. The direction of the split flips for QA, Math and Code.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests the fitted loss law in its synthetic-rewrite text-pretraining settings, not across the full range of language models, datasets, and training setups.
The 33.3× compute forecast is for the compute-limited Paloma setting; the study does not establish comparable extrapolation for other models or settings.

The study does not test both parameter and token growth in the data-limited setting, where target model size is fixed. Its compute-limited allocation results are fitted for particular evaluations and rewriting assumptions.
No fixed-parameter-count comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices is reported.
The tested extensions are synthetic rewriting and repeated natural-data exposure in text pretraining. Image/video modalities, fine-tuning, transfer, and other modalities are not tested.
The downstream evaluations are the paper’s QA, Math, and Code suites; it does not test a broad set of downstream tasks or model families.
The study tests sensitivity to data source, evaluation metric, repetition-penalty specification, and some surface-fitting assumptions, not every parameter-counting, schedule, data, or fitting choice.

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (pooled runs)
rows.size_stated: varied; compute-limited ladders and a 22B-parameter run
rows.operation_detail: Fit a loss surface over model parameters, training tokens, and rewrite fraction, using Chinchilla-style parameter and data terms.
rows.measure: Held-out loss fit and fitted compute-optimal loss frontier
rows.value: The model uses A/N^α + B/D^β plus a rewrite-dependent floor and an off-frontier curvature term. Fitted frontier: D*(C) = 4.5033 C^0.46447; L*(C, 0) = 0.80569 + 67.2942 C^-0.10963. Surface RMSE 0.01449 BPB, R² = 0.95, and relative error 1.1% over all runs.
rows.note: The reported loss law is not a single power law in every condition: rewrite fraction changes the loss floor, and an additional curvature term is used off the fitted frontier.
rows.check: Link and state are fine. The fit range is 3e18–3e20 FLOPs (about 2 orders of magnitude), and the 1e22 hero run is included as a frontier anchor. The form also adds a rewrite-dependent floor and an off-frontier curvature term. The implied Approach-3 exponents (α=0.205, β=0.236) are not in the row.

rows.subject: Qwen3 22B-parameter run
rows.operation_detail: Forecast held-out runs at 10^22 training FLOPs from a fit whose largest training budget was 3 × 10^20 FLOPs.
rows.measure: Relative error of predicted versus measured loss across the held-out rewrite fractions
rows.value: Mean error −1.04%; per-fraction range [−1.40, −0.85]%. The paper reports every measured loss was 0.9–1.4% below its forecast.
rows.note: The table reports the aggregate forecast error and range over the four held-out rewrite fractions.
rows.check: Correct. This is the forward forecast (refit through 3e20) from Table 8. Every measured loss sits below its forecast, so the forecasts err on the conservative side.

rows.subject: Qwen3 22B-parameter run
rows.operation_detail: Train at the predicted Paloma-optimal rewrite fraction and compare measured loss with the forecast.
rows.measure: Measured held-out BPB relative to scaling forecast
rows.baseline: Forecast loss; exact forecast value not stated
rows.value: Measured Paloma macro BPB 0.983; within 1.1% of the forecast.
rows.note: This is the held-out run at the predicted optimum.
rows.check: This is the single R=0.321 run already contained in r2's range. The main surface used this run as an anchor, so the 'within 1.1%' figure here should not be read as independent of r2's forward forecast.

source_check.correct: Tables 11–12 identify approximately 10^22 training FLOPs, with rewrite-generation compute additional. The run has 21.9B parameters, 76B tokens, R=0.321 and Paloma BPB 0.983. Figure 3 reports a −1.1% forward forecast error with this run held out; the final surface separately includes it as an anchor.

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (Paloma frontier)
rows.size_stated: varied; fitted allocation includes 22.39B parameters at 10^22 FLOPs
rows.operation_detail: Fit model-size and token-count compute-optimal frontiers.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal model-size and training-token allocation
rows.value: D*(C) ∝ C^0.46447; the corresponding model-size frontier is N*(C) = C/(6D*(C)), so model size grows as C^0.53553. At 10^22 FLOPs the fitted allocation is (N*, D*) = (22.39B, 74.44B).
rows.note: The fitted parameter frontier grows faster than the token frontier in this setup.
rows.check: Removed V7: a single frontier does not show fit-dependence. Eq. 30 gives N*=22.39B at 1e22, but Table 10's Paloma fit gives 23.5B/70.9B, and the trained run used 21.9B/76B; the row should note this discrepancy. The exponents (N∝C^0.54, D∝C^0.46) are close to the Hoffmann equal split, with model size growing slightly faster.

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (QA, Math, and Code frontiers)
rows.operation_detail: Fit evaluation-specific compute-optimal model-size and token-count frontiers.
rows.measure: Fitted N* and D* allocations
rows.value: At 10^22 FLOPs, Paloma: N* = 23.5B, D* = 70.9B; QA: 14.6B, 114.4B; Math: 14.2B, 117.2B; Code: 9.7B, 171.7B. The text reports QA has 1.5× the parameters of Code at this compute.
rows.note: The table also reports different task-specific allocations at 10^19 FLOPs; the optimal split depends on evaluation.
rows.check: Values are correct. Table 10 also shows tokens per parameter falling with compute for Paloma (5.5→3.0) but rising for QA (3.8→7.8), Math (7.3→8.2) and Code (11.5→17.7). Which of N or D grows faster therefore flips with the evaluation. The Paloma N* here (23.5B) differs from r4 (22.39B).

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (FineWeb-Edu and DCLM runs)
rows.operation_detail: Fit natural-only compute frontiers for two training corpora and fit the DCLM rewrite-fraction loss floor.
rows.measure: Token-frontier exponent and floor-optimal rewrite fraction
rows.value: DCLM D*(C) ∝ C^0.55091 versus FineWeb-Edu C^0.46447. On DCLM, fitted floor-optimal rewrite fraction is approximately 0.078, with a 0.00577-BPB gain over R = 0; the paper says its gain is smaller than on FineWeb-Edu.
rows.note: The DCLM rewrite sweeps do not charge rewrite-generation compute and estimate the floor optimum, not the compute-optimal rewrite fraction.
rows.check: The exponent difference (D* ∝ C^0.55 vs C^0.46; α 0.262 vs 0.205) comes with differently tuned hyperparameters per corpus and a sparse DCLM ladder. The DCLM rewrite-floor part (R*∞≈0.078) bears on no version.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix N.7, Equation 36 and DCLM rewrite-sweep paragraph: token exponent 0.55091; floor optimum 0.078; floor-fit RMSE 0.00162 BPB.

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (compute-limited rewrite sweeps)
rows.size_stated: varied; 583 runs in the allocation comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compare a shared compute-optimal token frontier across rewrite fractions with fraction-specific token frontiers.
rows.measure: Fit error and variation in fitted compute-optimal token count
rows.value: Allowing fraction-specific offsets lowers RMSE from 0.00831 to 0.00762 BPB; largest D*(R)/D*(0) shift is 1.196 at R = 0.8. A wild bootstrap rejects equal D* across fractions (p = 1/401).
rows.note: The text says this shift does not change the selected model size, and the shared model-size choice costs at most 0.0015 BPB on the per-R parabola.
rows.check: The dependence of D* on R is statistically significant but small: the largest ratio is 1.196, per-R exponents span 0.45–0.57, and the cost is ≤0.0015 BPB.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix M: RMSE 0.00831→0.00762 BPB; maximum D*(R)/D*(0)=1.196; p=1/401. Appendix N.1 gives per-R exponents 0.45–0.57 and shared-choice cost at most 0.0015 BPB.

rows.subject: Qwen3 dense models (compute-limited surface)
rows.operation_detail: Ablate the off-frontier curvature term while holding the floor and Chinchilla terms fixed.
rows.measure: Residual sum of squares and test of curvature restriction
rows.value: Removing curvature raises residual sum of squares from 0.0608 to 0.2726; likelihood-ratio statistic 1006.6.
rows.uncertainty: Architecture-wise wild bootstrap rejects the restriction, p = 1/401, with 400 draws.
rows.note: This result concerns off-frontier fit shape; the added term is constructed not to move the fitted compute-optimal frontier.
rows.check: This is an off-frontier misfit of the plain Chinchilla form. The curvature term leaves the frontier unchanged.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix N.1.6, Equations 31–32: residual sums of squares 0.0608→0.2726; likelihood-ratio statistic 1006.6; bootstrap p=1/401.

rows.subject: Qwen3 550M, 837M, 1B, and 3B target–rewriter pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compare alternative repetition-penalty forms in the data-limited loss fit.
rows.measure: Fit error and held-out forecast behavior
rows.value: The paper form has R² 0.959–0.985 across pairs. Removing the additive penalty raises RMSE by 1.8–3.4× and under-predicts held-out W = 24 by 0.8–3.8% on average. Freeing the repetition exponent lowers RMSE by at most 0.0005 BPB; the exponent is described as not identified. The dilution exponent s is weakly identified.
rows.note: The authors retain the linear penalty as the most parsimonious tested form and caution that rewrite-fraction extrapolation beyond W = 24 depends on weakly identified s.
rows.check: Added V5. Under repeated data, the plain power-law data term fails: no-penalty forms reach only R² 0.62–0.87 and push β to its bound.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix N.1.5, Table 9 and Figures 20–22: paper-form R² 0.959–0.985; removing the penalty raises RMSE 1.8–3.4×; penalty-free forms have R² approximately 0.62–0.87.
